subject: FintechX POC Observability plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: FintechX POC — post-call recap and next steps

Alex / Priya — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and agreed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC: 

Summary of needs:
- Low-latency, cost-predictable inference for transaction-scoring workloads (~1k qps peak).
- Strong observability: dashboards for latency/cost, tracing for end-to-end request flows, and log export for auditability.
- Data residency in us-west for initial trial.

Agreed POC scope & timeline:
- 3-week trial (Mar 22 — Apr 12) running a representative subset of workloads.
- Success criteria: avg p95 latency < 250ms for typical requests; no functional regressions vs your baseline; cost-per-1k-tokens within target band (we'll define exact numbers below).
- Deliverables: shared observability dashboard, weekly checkpoint calls, final evaluation report.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (project lead), Jordan (technical lead), Sean (SRE support).
- FintechX: Alex (product lead), Priya (platform/engineering).

Immediate next steps (action owners and dates):
1) Jordan to share the POC observability plan and initial dashboard wireframes by EOD 3/16 — ACTION: Jordan
2) FintechX to provide sample traffic profile + a low-sensitivity dataset for benchmarking by 3/18 — ACTION: Alex/Priya
3) Kickoff call to review environment access and runbook on 3/22 — ACTION: Marissa to schedule

I've attached a draft observability plan and a template for success criteria (spreadsheet). Please confirm or add any items I missed.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: 20270315-observability-plan.pdf (application/pdf), poc-success-criteria.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>

Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@fintechx.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FintechX POC — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Timeline: 3/22 kickoff works. We may need one extra week if onboarding our QA processes takes longer, but we'll try to stick to the 3-week window.
- Success criteria spreadsheet: I'll populate the expected cost targets and baseline latency numbers and share by 3/18.
- Observability: we need traces that map from our API gateway through Redwood to model inference latency, and we need exported logs that include request IDs and hashed user identifiers for audit.

Question for Jordan: do you have a preferred tracing header (e.g. W3C traceparent) and can Redwood export traces to our Datadog account?

I'll upload the sample traffic profile to the S3 link you provided in the drive folder by end of day Friday.

—Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Platform Engineering
FintechX
alex.johnson@fintechx.com | +1 (650) 555-9876

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-16T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FintechX POC — tracing / observability details

Alex — quick technical answers: 

- Tracing: Redwood supports W3C traceparent by default and can inject/propagate tracing headers end-to-end. We can forward traces to Datadog (OTLP) or export a filtered sampling to your account.
- Logs: we can stream structured logs (JSON) to an S3 bucket or to your Splunk/Datadog ingestion endpoint. Logs will include request_id, model_id, prompt_hash (if you prefer hashed PII), latency breakdowns (queue, compute, decode), and GPU utilization metrics.
- Dashboards: I'll attach a proposed dashboard wireframe (in the observability PDF) that includes the following tiles: overall throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate by route, KV-cache hit ratio, and model drift alert counts.

Notes on sampling & retention:
- We'll enable 100% tracing for sampled test traffic during the POC window and 10% for production-like burst traffic to control costs.
- Raw logs retention for the POC: 30 days by default; we can configure longer retention for compliance but that affects cost.

I'll get the updated observability plan and dashboard export links to you by EOD 3/16.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-16T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: FintechX POC — observability plan (attached) + kickoff scheduling

Alex / Priya — attached is the full observability plan (PDF) and the success criteria template (spreadsheet) updated with the items Jordan mentioned. Highlights from the plan: 

1) Dashboards & Metrics to monitor (real-time + historical):
   - Throughput (requests/sec) by route
   - Latency: p50/p95/p99 overall and broken down by queue/compute/decode
   - Cost metrics: cost per 1k tokens, GPU utilization, tokens-per-second
   - Error rate & error taxonomy by route (decoding errors, model errors, infra errors)
   - Cache metrics: KV-cache hit ratio, cache latency
   - Drift signals: model response distribution shifts against the baseline prompt set

2) Tracing & Log export:
   - W3C traceparent compatible headers; full traces for POC test runs (configurable sampling)
   - Structured JSON logs with request_id, masked_user_id, model_id, input_prompt_hash, latency_breakdown
   - Export targets: S3 (raw logs), Datadog (traces & metrics), and optional webhook for alerting

3) Alerting & SLAs for the POC:
   - Alert if p95 latency > 350ms for >5m sustained
   - Alert for error rate > 1% over a 10m window
   - Weekly health check with trimmed runbook for incident triage (Jordan/Sean on-call during ramp)

4) Evaluation plan & success criteria (how we'll measure pass/fail):
   - Performance: p95 < 250ms for representative workload; no functional regressions in output quality (sample prompt set)
   - Reliability: error rate < 0.5% during steady-state test windows
   - Cost: measured cost per 1k tokens within the band Alex provides; deviations >15% flagged for review

Next steps:
- Marissa to schedule kickoff for 3/22 (calendar invite to follow).
- Alex/Priya to upload sample traffic & baseline metrics by 3/18.
- Jordan to enable trace & log pipelines for the trial and share access instructions by 3/18.

Please review the attached and call out any changes to metrics or retention. If you approve, I'll mark the POC scope as final and we can lock scheduling.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: 20270315-observability-plan.pdf, poc-success-criteria.xlsx

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>

Subject: Re: FintechX POC — observability plan (attached) + kickoff scheduling

Thanks Marissa — plan looks good. A couple quick asks before kickoff: 

- Please set the default trace sampling for test runs to 100% and provide a guide for switching to lower sampling after the POC.
- Can Redwood push alerts to our Datadog account and also send critical alerts to our Slack #platform-alerts channel?

We will upload the sample traffic and baseline numbers by 3/18 and confirm kickoff for 3/22 once we have the runbook.

Appreciate the clear owners and timelines — looking forward to the trial.

—Alex
